D005-D007_h001.question:
"Lately, it feels like the world is just... crumbling. I see the signs, you know? The news reports, it's all part of it. I've been seeing things too, shadows in my peripheral vision, sometimes clear as day I'll see people, they are not there, they are trying to warn me that something terrible is coming, their faces are grim. It's been going on for about two months now, this sense that everything's going to collapse.

My wife, she's worried. She says I've been down, and yeah, I've felt pretty low, like there's no point in anything. But that feeling, that sadness, it started a little after all the other stuff, the seeing and the believing the world is ending. It's not like the depression has been hanging around consistently, though. It kind of comes and goes, especially when I'm really consumed with the idea that the world is about to end. It’s pretty distressing, and it doesn't stick around as long as these visions and beliefs that are constantly on my mind."
D005-D007_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h002.question: Lately, things have been… off. For the past two months, it feels like I’m constantly being watched. Every transaction I make, every trade—I just *know* there are shadowy groups trying to track my movements, trying to steal my crypto. And the taste… god, the taste. This really foul, metallic bitterness is often in my mouth, even after I've brushed my teeth; it comes and goes without warning, and it’s always worse when the surveillance feelings kick in. I’ve also felt really down in the dumps, a deep sadness that's been hanging over me. It started about six weeks ago, right after the whole 'being watched' thing started to escalate, but to be honest, those really bad, dark feelings only lasted for a couple of weeks at most. The constant fear of being targeted, that's still very much here, even though the intense sadness has thankfully lightened up quite a bit.
D005-D007_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h003.question:
"Lately, it's like my own body is betraying me. I'm utterly convinced my internal organs are rotting, turning to mush inside, even though every doctor tells me I'm fine. It's been going on for about two months now. And the taste... oh god, the taste. Everything tastes like stale pennies and decay, even my favorite coffee. It's constant, a metallic, putrid flavor that just won't go away.

I know it sounds wild, but it feels so real. This all really kicked off about two months ago. Before that, I had a period, maybe a couple of weeks, where I felt really down, useless, couldn't focus on work. But honestly, those intense sad feelings have mostly faded into the background now. Now it's just this constant, terrifying feeling that my insides are disintegrating, and that awful taste."
D005-D007_h003.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h004.question:
Lately, things have been… off. It started about two months ago, maybe a little more, when I began noticing a really distinct, awful metallic taste in my mouth, almost like old pennies, even after brushing my teeth or eating. It's constant. And then it's this overwhelming feeling that everything is just falling apart. I can't shake the conviction that the world, as we know it, is actually ending. It’s not just a feeling, it’s a certainty, like a catastrophe is already underway. My art used to be my escape, but now even that feels pointless.

I know it sounds crazy, but it’s real to me. For the past few weeks, I’ve also just felt so incredibly down, no energy, no interest in anything, barely eating. It's a heavy, dark cloud. But honestly, even before this deep sadness hit me, the metallic taste and the overwhelming sense of impending doom were already there, strong as ever, for a good while. The despair is definitely making everything worse now, but those other things came first and just sort of... persisted, on their own.
D005-D007_h004.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h005.question: I know it sounds… strange, but I truly believe my boss, Mark, is in love with me. It’s not just a crush on my part – I've seen the way he looks at me. He leaves little notes on my desk, sometimes just a doodle, other times a vague compliment about my work, and I just *know* it's his way of secretly communicating his affection. When I’m alone, I hear his voice, sometimes whispering my name, sometimes telling me how talented I am, even when he’s not around. It's been going on for about two months now. Things feel a bit harder than usual, like I'm in a fog. Some days, I just don't want to get out of bed, and the bright colors I usually love in my designs just look dull. I've felt pretty down for the last few weeks, almost as long as the voices and the feelings about Mark started. I had a really rough patch where I couldn't focus on anything, just felt numb and hopeless, but that only lasted a little while. The voices and Mark’s "messages," though, those haven't stopped at all.
D005-D007_h005.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D007_h006.question: It’s been almost seven months now, and I just don't feel right. My body… it’s like my insides are rotting, that my organs are all shriveled up and dead. No doctor believes me, but I can feel it. When people talk, sometimes their words just get stuck in my head and I repeat them without meaning to. I’ve barely worked my taxi in months, what’s the point? Nothing brings me joy anymore, not fishing, not even seeing my kids. For a few weeks there, maybe two or three months ago, I was feeling really low, just like I couldn't get out of bed. But that passed. The body thing, though, and the other stuff, that’s still going strong.
D005-D007_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h007.question: "It all started about seven months ago, maybe a bit more. I began to feel this… strangeness within my body. Like my internal organs, especially my kidneys, weren't filtering right, that they were rotting inside me. I know it sounds absurd, but it feels so real, so *wrong*. It’s hard to describe, but sometimes I find myself holding peculiar positions for long stretches, almost as if I'm trying to keep everything from falling apart or moving around inside. My husband tries to talk to me, to connect, but I just can't seem to emote like I used to. The light has gone out of things, and I feel so flat, so empty. I’ve had some low spells lately, feeling really down and tearful, but those only started a couple of months ago, long after the other stuff set in, and they come and go. It’s the other bizarre sensations and the feeling of being frozen, that’s been the constant. It’s been really affecting my work as a lawyer, I can barely focus."
D005-D007_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h008.question:
"It’s been an uphill battle for the last seven months, doctor. I just don’t understand why things feel so off. My husband, bless his heart, says I’m just 'not myself.' I’ve noticed I barely speak anymore; it's like my thoughts are stuck, and getting words out feels impossible. I used to be so articulate, running the franchise, but now conversations just...stop.

The hardest part has been this overwhelming belief that the new delivery driver, Mark, is madly in love with me. He just got a new ring, and I know it's a secret message to me, a declaration of his unspoken feelings. I’ve tried to subtly show him I reciprocate by doing these weird little arm gestures when he’s around – almost like a secret code. My team thinks I’m just being eccentric, but I know better.

There have also been times, maybe a month or so back, when I felt utterly worthless, couldn’t get out of bed, and lost all interest in the business. But that only lasted a few weeks, nothing like the constant pressure of Mark’s ‘secret love’ or this quietness that's taken over me. The depression passed, but these other things just… linger, like they’re part of me now."
D005-D007_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h009.question:
Lately, things have been… off. It started about seven months ago. I've become convinced my husband, Arthur, is having an affair with one of the new volunteers at the museum. I see them talking, and I just *know* it means something more, even though he swears it’s not true. He says I'm imagining things, but it feels so real, like a knot in my stomach.

And honestly, I haven't been myself. People say I seem flat, like my emotions are muted. When guests ask questions, my face doesn't seem to react the way it used to, and my voice sounds monotone. Sometimes I find myself holding unusual poses, like my arm will stay straight out for a long time, and I don't even realize how odd it looks until someone points it out.

I've been feeling pretty down too, a deep sadness that's been there for a good part of the seven months. It wasn’t there for the whole time, though. There was a period of a few weeks where I felt this intense certainty about Arthur, and the other things were happening, but I wasn't feeling that heavy sadness. But then it came back again. It just feels like there’s a wall between me and the world.
D005-D007_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h010.question:
"Lately, I just haven't been myself. For about seven months now, things have felt… off. Every time the radio plays a certain song, or I see a specific color car, it feels like a signal, a message just for me that others don't get. It’s hard to explain, but it’s like the universe is talking to me through everyday objects.

My ex-husband thinks I'm going crazy, and honestly, sometimes I wonder. I've stopped really talking much because it feels like my thoughts just get stuck; the words won't come out right. When people try to move my arm, like to hand me something, it’s like there’s this strange, soft push-back, almost like I'm a mannequin.

I know I’ve been down lately – really low mood, terrible sleep, just can’t seem to find the energy to even start on my furniture commissions. But those feelings of darkness and sadness only snuck in a couple of months ago, long after the other stuff started. The weird messages and the way my speech has changed, that's been constant. I only feel depressed for short bursts, and then I go right back to feeling those odd connections and having trouble speaking, regardless of my mood."
D005-D007_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D007_h011.question:
Honestly, everything feels like it's falling apart. My boyfriend, Mark, who I’ve been with for five years, is definitely cheating on me. I see the signs everywhere—the way he checks his phone, the subtle smiles. Even when he’s just talking to his guy friends, I know he’s really planning to meet someone else. I’ve tried to ignore it, but I can’t. I keep pushing my hair behind my ears and then patting it down, almost like I’m trying to smooth things over, but it doesn’t help.

This started about four months ago, and I barely sleep now. There was a time, maybe a month or so back, when I felt utterly hopeless, like the world was closing in on me. I lost my appetite and couldn't even focus on my civil service exam prep, which is everything to me. But that severe low mood, it passed after a few weeks. The cheating... that belief is constant. It won't go away. I just wish I could trust him again, or at least understand why he's doing this to me.
D005-D007_h011.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h012.question: It's been about four months now that things have felt… off. I’ve started noticing that the streamers I watch, and even the bugs I log at work – it all feels like it’s subtly about me, or hinting at me somehow. Like there’s a secret message just under the surface, specially for me. Sometimes my face just… twists up, you know? Like I'm making weird expressions without even meaning to, and I only notice when someone looks at me strangely. I’ve been feeling really down, too, for most of that time, just completely drained and uninterested in anything, even my games. But these past few weeks, the depressive gloom actually lifted for a bit, maybe a week or two, which was a relief. The strange thoughts and the facial movements, though, those didn't go away at all; they’ve been constant for the whole four months.
D005-D007_h012.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h013.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a tough few months, maybe four months now since things really started going downhill. I’m here because my wife, bless her heart, she says I'm not myself and she's worried. She says I've been acting strangely, and I suppose she's right.

It’s just… I know she’s been seeing someone else. I see how she looks at me, and I just know it. She denies it, of course, but it's clear as day. I've tried to talk to her, to get her to admit it, but she just gets upset.

And honestly, I just can't be bothered with anything anymore. Getting up in the morning for my janitor job, it’s a monumental effort. My wife will ask me to take out the trash or help with chores, and I just… I can’t. I just stand there, sometimes I don’t even answer her. It's not that I don't hear her, I just can't bring myself to do it.

There have been times, a few weeks here and there, where I've felt pretty low, really down in the dumps, no energy, feeling hopeless. But that kind of deep sadness usually passes within a few weeks and I am still having these thoughts about my wife. The other stuff, the thoughts about my wife and just feeling like I can't move, that’s been pretty constant for over four months now."
D005-D007_h013.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h014.question:
"It's been... I'd say about four months now that things have felt truly off. I'm here because my sister, she's worried. She says I've been different. I keep telling her, the world isn't going to last much longer, you know? It's all falling apart, everything we build, it's just…dust. Sometimes, I find myself just rocking back and forth, or tapping my fingers on my leg without even realizing it until someone points it out.

At first, a few months ago, I was really down, profoundly sad and losing interest in everything, even teaching, which I used to love. That feeling lasted for maybe a month or so, tops. It was intense for a while, but then it started to lift, and now it's just these other things, these bizarre thoughts about the end of the world, and all these strange movements that have become the real problem. The sadness isn't the main issue anymore; it's these other thoughts and behaviors that have really taken over and haven't gone away."
D005-D007_h014.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h015.question:
"Everything just feels… off, doctor. It started subtly, maybe four months ago. I’d be in the lab, and I'd swear the data on my screen, even just little flickering pixels, was trying to tell me something specific, personalized. Like the research was suddenly all about me, a secret code embedded for my eyes only. And then, when my husband tries to help me move, if he guides my arm, it's like it just stays there. Like it needs his push to tell it it can move again.

I've also been feeling really down, honestly, for a bit before the really intense, strange stuff started. Just a heavy cloud, no energy, losing interest in my bioinformatics work. But those feelings, the low mood, that's eased up lately even though these… these peculiar beliefs and experiences, they're still here, front and center. The delusions and the weird stiffness in my body, they haven’t budged even as the sadness has lifted. It’s like the dark mood was only around for a little while, but these other things, they’re really sticking."
D005-D007_h015.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h016.question:
"Truth be told, doctor, things have been feeling… off. It started a few months back, maybe three months now. This woman, she’s a clerk down at the co-op… she’s been sending me messages. Not with words, not directly, but with her eyes, the way she smiles, little gestures. She’s in love with me, I know it. It’s like she’s trying to communicate in a secret language only we understand. It’s hard to explain, but sometimes I hear voices too, whispering her name, telling me to ‘harvest the sky-fruit.’ I know it sounds strange, that last part, but it makes sense to me.

For a bit there, a month or so ago, I felt real down, no energy for anything, even the farm work felt pointless. My wife noticed it too, kept asking if I was alright. But that feeling’s mostly passed now. I still feel pretty flat, though, nothing really brings me joy like it used to. Even when the crops do well, I don’t get that satisfaction. It’s just… gone. But the feelings about this woman, and the voices, they’re still there, strong as ever, and have been for these past few months. That bleakness was just a passing shadow, didn't last anywhere near as long as this other business."
D005-D007_h016.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h017.question: I’m here because things have been… off. At work, I just can’t bring myself to do anything. Even simple tasks feel like a monumental effort, and I just sit there staring at my computer. It's been like this for about three months now. And the agency, I know they're watching me, trying to find a reason to fire me. They’ve even put something in my food, a weird bitter taste that nobody else seems to notice. I try to tell my supervisor, but then I lose my train of thought, and I end up talking about… well, not what I meant to. It’s hard to focus. I've been feeling down, profoundly sad since my husband passed, but honestly, this feeling of being watched and those awful tastes… they’ve been around longer than the recent low mood, or at least they’re still here even when I have a few good days. It’s like the sadness comes and goes, but these other things, they’re constant.
D005-D007_h017.options:
A. Schizophrenia

    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h018.question:
Lately, things have been really off. I feel like I've got this incredible power, like I can pretty much read people's minds and predict their next move in the gym. It's like I'm destined for something huge, way bigger than just training clients. But then, I'll be talking, and my thoughts just… drift. One minute I'm explaining a bicep curl, the next I'm thinking about the migratory patterns of birds, and it's hard to get back on track.

It's been about three months now. And these sensations… I keep feeling things crawling on me, under my skin. Like tiny bugs, even when there's nothing there. It makes me jumpy. And I know I don't show it much, but inside I'm a mess. My clients sometimes ask if I'm okay because I guess my face doesn't show much, and my voice sounds pretty flat. For a little bit there, about a month ago, I felt really down, like the world was closing in, but that wave of sadness passed pretty quickly. It wasn't like that for long, just a couple of weeks, then it went away, but all the other stuff, the thoughts and feelings, they just kept going strong.
D005-D007_h018.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h019.question: It's been… I don't know, a good three months now, maybe a little more, that things have really taken a turn for the strange. I keep getting these clear messages, usually a woman's voice, telling me how much she adores me, believes I'm her soulmate. It’s comforting, but also unsettling because I don’t know who it is. My sermons used to be so clear, but lately, it's like my thoughts are all tangled, coming out as "the steeple, the flock, the light, the dark, it all… is… you see?" My wife says I don't show much emotion anymore, just sort of flattened, even when I *feel* things keenly inside. I tried to explain to my wife just this past week, about the voices and how I am the chosen one, but she mentioned how I had seemed rather melancholic and withdrawn for about a month or so before that, like I almost never left the bed unless it was absolutely essential. I also remember struggling with sleep and just feeling utterly hopeless. But then, as the voices got louder and more dominant, that heavy feeling, it just… lifted. It’s primarily the voices and the feeling of divine connection that are constant now.
D005-D007_h019.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h020.question: Lately, things have been really tough. It feels like my brain is playing tricks on me. I’ve been hearing voices, not all the time, but usually when I’m alone in my apartment. They don’t say anything awful, more like they’re cheering me on, telling me I’m destined for really big things—like I have a special gift for understanding the internet that no one else does, and I'm going to invent the next big app. It’s hard to stay focused on work, though. My mind just jumps all over the place. I’ll start talking about a client, then suddenly I’m thinking about algorithms, then what I had for lunch yesterday, it's just a mess. My boss keeps asking why my updates are so short, but honestly, I just don't have much to say anymore. I used to be so chatty online and in person. This has been going on for about three months now. D005-D007_h021.question:
It's been… I don’t even know how long, maybe three months now, that things have felt so off. I know for a fact I have a special gift, a sort of insight into how the digital world is truly structured. I can see the code behind everything, glowing lines and figures that others just can't perceive. Sometimes, these figures, they take on forms, almost like people, sitting right there at my desk with me, watching me design.

My husband tries to get me to do things, simple things like helping out with dinner, but sometimes I just… can't. It's not that I don't want to; it’s like my body won’t respond, as if there’s a wall between what I want to do and what I actually do. People think I'm just being stubborn, but it's more than that. I've felt pretty down sometimes, really low, finding it hard to get going for a few days here and there. But those feelings usually pass; it's these other things – the visions, this knowledge I have – that stick around, no matter how I’m feeling. They’ve been here, consistently, for the whole three months, even when my mood isn't in the dumps.

D005-D007_h022.question:

I’ll be sketching a design, and suddenly, I’ll swear her eyes are staring at me from the corner of the room, or I’ll catch a glimpse of her shadow just as I turn my head. D005-D007_h024.question:

D005-D007_h025.question:
